If you are seriously interested in this kind of stuff, you need to read 1984 by George Orwell.

I know the book gets tossed around a lot and people are quick to throw around the term "Orwellian", but it is a seriously good book.

The story is just a means of demonstrating how control of language and language manipulation can be used to control real world events.

If you can control the language, and change it in your favor, you can shape how people talk about issues, how people frame discussions. Just like the question "So how often do you beat your wife" has the built-in assumption that you bear your wife, you can build in assumptions to other conversations. If you can bend language, you can bend the assumptions built into conversations and make sure they're the assumptions you want people to have.

It's really crazy and scary. Orwell was on the front lines in a time and place in the world where communism and fascism were just gaining power, and anarchism had a flash in the pan bright spot in Spain. He existed at this unique point to watch how political movements interacted and ate each other, and how language and propaganda was used.

If you want a better awareness of how language is used in politics to try and control outcomes, seriously read this book.
